line: Sit, before the sun finishes you. New people always stare at the walls. Look at the tree instead. Everything Ward has ever bled for is down under those roots.
transcript: Sit before the sun finishes you. New people always stare at the walls. Look at the tree instead. Everything Ward has ever bled for is down under those roots

line: Still breathing? Good. Sit. Old women and old cities both like to be asked about themselves.
transcript: Still breathing? Good. Sit. Old women and old cities both like to be asked about themselves

line: Water. The only sure well for hundreds of kilometres. The company built here for the ore, back when Tir was a line in somebody's accounts. They dug it, shaped it, shipped it off-world. Then one season, the ships didn't come.
transcript: Water. The only sure well for hundreds of kilometers. The company built here for the ore, back when Tia was a line in somebody's accounts. They dug it, shaped it, shipped it off-world. Then one season, the ships didn't come

line: Nobody told the machines. Some kept digging for masters long dead. Others decided we were in the way, or that we were ore. The cities went dark, one, then the next, then all of them. That's what we call the Fall.
transcript: Nobody told the machines. Some kept digging for masters long dead. Others decided we were in the way, or that we were ore. The cities went dark, one, then the next, then all of them. That's what we call the Fall.

line: They forgot us. They fenced us off for fear of the machines. Or they had it worse. I've heard all three sworn as truth, and never by anyone who'd know. The women of my family set out a cup for the supply pilot. It has been dry for centuries, and I still wash it.

line: Out of spite, mostly. One greenhouse, one nanofab, a few machines that stayed loyal. Then we woke the Quantum Tubes. Goods pulled to dust here and knitted whole at the far end. After that, dead nodes began waking on their own. Ask an engineer why, and watch them change the subject.

line: The Karaveen. When the cities fell they took to the sand, and for a lifetime they were the only thread between one well and the next. The Tubes made them needless. Still they go. There are people out there no Tube will ever reach, and the Karaveen know their children's names.

line: The Wardens. They began as neighbours taking turns on the wall. Now some have more lattice in them than bone, and scraps of old machine minds to steady the gun. I've washed three of them for burial. They are the wall that has never been allowed to fall.
transcript: The wardens. They began as neighbors taking turns on the wall. Now some have more lattice in them than bone and scraps of old machine minds to steady the gun. I've washed three of them for burial. They are the wall that has never been allowed to fall.

line: The Outer Berms. Factories to the horizon, once. Now it's their bones, and whatever still walks about inside them. There are secrets under that scrap. Few go looking, and fewer come home. So don't go out in just a shirt. Mira sells a vest and boots. Better plate, you build.

line: There's a red container on the south wall, behind the Nanofab yard. The family left with a Karaveen caravan and made the bunk before they went. That's how you know they won't be back. Forty credits, and I write your name on the roll. In Ward that's worth more than the key. It means somebody counts you.

line: There. Written. The door knows you now, and so does the city. If you don't come home from the Berms some night, someone will notice. Out here, that's most of what a home is.
